question_html: What is the legal status of a debenture holder in a company?

options.A: Owner of the company
options.B: Creditor of the company
options.C: Partner of the company
options.D: Guarantor of the company

answer_html: Answer: (B) A debenture is an instrument acknowledging a debt, making a debenture holder a creditor of the company[cite: 16].

question_html: Under Section 71(2) of the Companies Act, 2013, can a company issue debentures carrying voting rights?

options.A: Yes, if approved by a special resolution.
options.B: No company can issue any debentures which carry any voting rights[cite: 16].
options.C: Yes, for fully convertible debentures only.
options.D: Yes, if authorized by the Articles of Association.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Section 71(2) provides that no company can issue any debentures which carry any voting rights[cite: 16].

question_html: What type of resolution is required under Section 71(1) for issuing debentures with an option to convert them into shares?

options.A: Ordinary Resolution
options.B: Special Resolution passed at a duly convened general meeting[cite: 16]
options.C: Board Resolution only
options.D: Unanimous Resolution of directors

answer_html: Answer: (B) The issue of such debentures with an option to convert into shares should be approved by a special resolution passed at a duly convened general meeting[cite: 16].

question_html: For other unlisted companies (other than AIFIs, Banking Companies, NBFCs, and HFCs), what is the required adequacy percentage for Debenture Redemption Reserve (DRR)?

options.A: 5% of the value of outstanding debentures issued[cite: 16]
options.B: 10% of the value of outstanding debentures issued[cite: 16]
options.C: 25% of the value of outstanding debentures issued
options.D: 50% of the value of outstanding debentures issued

answer_html: Answer: (B) For other unlisted companies, DRR shall be 10% of the value of the outstanding debentures issued[cite: 16].

question_html: Are All India Financial Institutions (AIFIs) regulated by RBI and Banking Companies required to create any Debenture Redemption Reserve (DRR) for privately placed or public debentures?

options.A: Yes, 10% DRR is mandatory.
options.B: Yes, 25% DRR is mandatory.
options.C: No DRR is required[cite: 16].
options.D: DRR is required only for public issues.

answer_html: Answer: (C) No DRR is required for AIFIs and Banking Companies for both public as well as privately placed debentures[cite: 16].

question_html: What is the specified deadline and minimum percentage for deposit or investment of funds by companies required to invest in respect of debentures maturing during the year ending 31st March of the next year?

options.A: On or before 30th April, not less than 15% of the amount of its debentures maturing during the year[cite: 16]
options.B: On or before 31st March, not less than 10% of maturing debentures
options.C: On or before 30th June, not less than 25% of maturing debentures
options.D: On or before 31st December, not less than 50% of maturing debentures

answer_html: Answer: (A) Companies shall on or before the 30th day of April in each year deposit or invest a sum not less than 15% of the amount of its debentures maturing during the year[cite: 16].

question_html: To which account is the balance of the Debenture Redemption Reserve (DRR) transferred after all debentures are fully redeemed?

options.A: Capital Reserve Account
options.B: General Reserve Account[cite: 16]
options.C: Profit and Loss Account
options.D: Securities Premium Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) After redemption of debentures, DRR should be transferred to general reserve[cite: 16].
topic_text: Transfer of DRR to General Reserve

question_html: Which of the following methods of redemption of debentures is explicitly excluded from the CA Foundation syllabus?

options.A: Payment in lumpsum
options.B: Payment in instalments
options.C: Purchase of debentures in open market[cite: 16]
options.D: Conversion into shares

answer_html: Answer: (C) Purchase of debentures in open market is not covered in the chapter as it has been specifically excluded from the syllabus at Foundation level[cite: 16].

question_html: XYZ Ltd. issued 1,000, 12% convertible debentures of ₹100 each redeemable at 5% premium with an option to convert 20% into equity shares of ₹10 each at ₹20 per share. If 20,000 worth of debentures opted for conversion, how many equity shares are issued?

options.A: 1,000 shares
options.B: 210 shares[cite: 16]
options.C: 400 shares
options.D: 2,000 shares

answer_html: Answer: (B) Redemption value of 40 debentures (20% of 200 debentures) at 5% premium = $40 \times \text{₹}105 = \text{₹}4,200$. Shares issued at ₹20 each = $\text{₹}4,200 / \text{₹}20 = 210$ shares[cite: 16].

question_html: What authority can direct a company to redeem debentures forthwith if it fails to redeem them on maturity or pay interest?

options.A: Registrar of Companies (RoC)
options.B: The Tribunal (NCLT)[cite: 16]
options.C: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
options.D: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)

answer_html: Answer: (B) Where a company fails to redeem debentures or pay interest, the Tribunal may direct the company to redeem debentures forthwith upon application[cite: 16].

question_html: Which of the following statements is true regarding debentures?

options.A: A debenture holder is an owner of the company.
options.B: A debenture holder can get his money back only on liquidation.
options.C: A debenture issued at a discount can be redeemed at a premium[cite: 16].
options.D: Debentures carry voting rights in general meetings.

answer_html: Answer: (C) A debenture issued at a discount can indeed be redeemed at a premium, as terms of issue dictate[cite: 16].

question_html: Are listed NBFCs and listed Housing Finance Companies (HFCs) required to create a Debenture Redemption Reserve (DRR)?

options.A: Yes, 10% DRR is required.
options.B: Yes, 25% DRR is required.
options.C: No DRR is required for both public and privately placed debentures[cite: 16].
options.D: DRR is required only for public issues.

answer_html: Answer: (C) All listed NBFCs and listed HFCs require no DRR for both public as well as privately placed debentures[cite: 16].
topic_text: DRR for Listed NBFCs and HFCs

question_html: In what permitted methods can the 15% DRR investment be held?

options.A: Deposits with scheduled banks, government securities, trust securities, or bonds notified under Section 20 of Indian Trusts Act[cite: 16]
options.B: Equity shares of subsidiary companies
options.C: Unsecured loans to directors
options.D: Inventories and trade receivables

answer_html: Answer: (A) Investments must be in scheduled bank deposits, government securities, Indian Trusts Act Section 20 securities, or notified bonds[cite: 16].

question_html: What is the accounting entry for setting aside a fixed amount of profit for Debenture Redemption Reserve?

options.A: Profit and Loss A/c Dr. To Debenture Redemption Reserve A/c[cite: 16]
options.B: Debenture Redemption Reserve A/c Dr. To Profit and Loss A/c
options.C: Bank A/c Dr. To Debenture Redemption Reserve A/c
options.D: Debentures A/c Dr. To DRR A/c

answer_html: Answer: (A) Profit and Loss Account is debited and Debenture Redemption Reserve Account is credited[cite: 16].

question_html: What entry is passed when Debenture Redemption Reserve Investments are purchased?

options.A: Debenture Redemption Reserve Investment A/c Dr. To Bank A/c[cite: 16]
options.B: Bank A/c Dr. To DRR Investment A/c
options.C: DRR A/c Dr. To Bank A/c
options.D: Investment A/c Dr. To DRR A/c

answer_html: Answer: (A) Debenture Redemption Reserve Investment A/c is debited and Bank A/c is credited[cite: 16].

question_html: How is interest received on Debenture Redemption Reserve Investments treated in the absence of re-investment?

options.A: Credited directly to DRR Account
options.B: Credited to Profit and Loss Account[cite: 16]
options.C: Credited to Capital Reserve Account
options.D: Credited to Securities Premium Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) Interest received is taken to Profit and Loss Account when not re-invested[cite: 16].

question_html: What entry is passed when the amount due on redemption becomes payable to debentureholders?

options.A: Debentures A/c Dr. To Debentureholders A/c[cite: 16]
options.B: Debentureholders A/c Dr. To Bank A/c
options.C: Bank A/c Dr. To Debentures A/c
options.D: DRR A/c Dr. To Debentures A/c

answer_html: Answer: (A) Debentures Account is debited and Debentureholders Account is credited when amount is due[cite: 16].

question_html: Paradise Ltd. (unlisted non-NBFC/HFC) had 12% Debentures of ₹7,50,000 and a DRR balance of ₹25,000. What additional amount must be transferred to DRR before redemption?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Total DRR required = 10% of ₹7,50,000 = ₹75,000. Available balance = ₹25,000. Additional amount = ₹75,000 - ₹25,000 = ₹50,000[cite: 16].

question_html: What does 'Payment in lumpsum' method of redemption signify?

options.A: Payment of the entire debenture is made in one lot at maturity or expiry of a specified period[cite: 16]
options.B: Payment is made in equal monthly instalments over 10 years.
options.C: Debentures are converted into shares gradually.
options.D: Debentures are bought back daily from open market.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Under lumpsum payment, payment of the entire debenture is made in one lot at maturity or before[cite: 16].

question_html: What does 'Payment in instalments' method entail?

options.A: Payment of specified portion of debenture is made in instalments at specified intervals[cite: 16]
options.B: Payment of entire debenture in one lump sum.
options.C: Conversion of all debentures into equity on day one.
options.D: Forfeiture of debentures due to non-payment of calls.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Payment of specified portion of debenture is made in instalments at specified intervals[cite: 16].

question_html: A company had issued 20,000, 13% debentures of ₹100 each, redeemable at 5% premium with an option to convert 20% into equity shares at ₹15 per share (Face value ₹10). If debenture holders holding 2,500 debentures did not exercise the option, how many equity shares are allotted to those exercising the option to the maximum?

options.A: 21,000 shares
options.B: 24,500 shares[cite: 16]
options.C: 35,000 shares
options.D: 17,500 shares

answer_html: Answer: (B) Debentures opting for conversion = 20,000 - 2,500 = 17,500. 20% of 17,500 = 3,500 debentures. Redemption value at 5% premium = $3,500 \times \text{₹}105 = \text{₹}3,67,500$. Shares at ₹15 each = $\text{₹}3,67,500 / \text{₹}15 = 24,500$ shares[cite: 16].

question_html: What is the purpose of creating a trusteeship in favour of one or more persons in the case of mortgage debentures?

options.A: To safeguard the interest of debenture holders with powers of a mortgagee[cite: 16]
options.B: To manage daily manufacturing operations
options.C: To audit the annual financial statements
options.D: To determine equity dividend rates

answer_html: Answer: (A) Trustees have powers of a mortgagee of a property and act to safeguard the interest of debenture holders[cite: 16].

question_html: Can amounts credited to the Debenture Redemption Reserve be utilized by the company for any purpose other than the redemption of debentures?

options.A: Yes, for paying dividends if profits are low.
options.B: No, it should not be utilized for any purpose other than the redemption of debentures[cite: 16].
options.C: Yes, for issuing fully paid bonus shares.
options.D: Yes, for writing off preliminary expenses.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Amount credited to DRR account should not be utilised for any purpose other than the redemption of debentures[cite: 16].

question_html: What source of profit is used to create the Debenture Redemption Reserve?

options.A: Profits of the company available for payment of dividend[cite: 16]
options.B: Capital reserve arising from asset revaluation
options.C: Securities premium collected on share issues
options.D: Forfeited shares account balance

answer_html: Answer: (A) DRR is created out of the profits of the company available for payment of dividend[cite: 16].

question_html: In the case of partly convertible debentures, how should the Debenture Redemption Reserve be created?

options.A: DRR shall be created in respect of the entire debenture issue.
options.B: DRR shall be created in respect of the non-convertible portion of the debenture issue[cite: 16].
options.C: DRR shall be created in respect of the convertible portion only.
options.D: No DRR is required for partly convertible debentures.

answer_html: Answer: (B) In case of partly convertible debentures, DRR shall be created in respect of non-convertible portion of debenture issue[cite: 16].

question_html: What entry is passed when encashment of Debenture Redemption Reserve Investments takes place?

options.A: Bank A/c Dr. To Debenture Redemption Reserve Investment A/c[cite: 16]
options.B: DRR Investment A/c Dr. To Bank A/c
options.C: Bank A/c Dr. To DRR A/c
options.D: Debentureholders A/c Dr. To Bank A/c

answer_html: Answer: (A) Bank A/c is debited and Debenture Redemption Reserve Investment A/c is credited upon encashment[cite: 16].
topic_text: Journal Entry for Encashment of DRRI

question_html: What entry is passed when payment is made to debentureholders upon redemption?

options.A: Debentureholders A/c Dr. To Bank A/c[cite: 16]
options.B: Bank A/c Dr. To Debentureholders A/c
options.C: Debentures A/c Dr. To Bank A/c
options.D: Debentureholders A/c Dr. To DRR A/c

answer_html: Answer: (A) Debentureholders Account is debited and Bank Account is credited upon payment[cite: 16].
topic_text: Journal Entry for Payment to Debentureholders

question_html: Why is a charge created on assets when issuing mortgage debentures?

options.A: To provide security to debenture holders regarding repayment of principal and interest[cite: 16]
options.B: To increase the authorized share capital of the company
options.C: To avoid corporate income tax liabilities
options.D: To comply with stock exchange listing fee rules

answer_html: Answer: (A) A charge is created on assets to secure the debt and safeguard debenture holders[cite: 16].

question_html: What is the legal validity status of a charge created on company assets if it is not registered with the Registrar of Companies?

options.A: It is completely valid and binding.
options.B: The charge is not valid unless registered with the Registrar[cite: 16].
options.C: It is valid only for the first 30 days.
options.D: It requires NCLT confirmation to become valid.

answer_html: Answer: (B) The charge is not valid unless registered with the Registrar, and his certificate is printed on the bond[cite: 16].

question_html: What does an instrument issued by a company under its seal acknowledging a debt represent?

options.A: A Share Certificate
options.B: A Debenture[cite: 16]
options.C: A Bill of Lading
options.D: A Certificate of Incorporation

answer_html: Answer: (B) A debenture is an instrument issued under seal acknowledging a debt[cite: 16].

question_html: Which companies are exempt from creating a Debenture Redemption Reserve (DRR) under Rule 18(7)?

options.A: All unlisted manufacturing companies
options.B: All India Financial Institutions (AIFIs), Banking companies, listed NBFCs, listed HFCs, and other listed companies[cite: 16]
options.C: Only private companies with paid-up capital under ₹1 crore
options.D: Companies with zero debt

answer_html: Answer: (B) AIFIs, Banking companies, listed NBFCs, listed HFCs, and other listed companies are exempt from creating DRR[cite: 16].

question_html: What is the primary objective of establishing a Debenture Redemption Reserve and making DRR investments?

options.A: To ensure the company has sufficient liquid funds and profits for the timely redemption of debentures[cite: 16]
options.B: To distribute tax-free dividends to equity shareholders
options.C: To write off accumulated operating losses
options.D: To pay managerial remuneration

answer_html: Answer: (A) DRR and its investments ensure the company will have sufficient liquid funds for redemption when due[cite: 16].

question_html: When debentures are redeemed at a premium, how is the premium payable on redemption treated in the accounts in the absence of specific multi-year terms?

options.A: Charged to Profit and Loss Account of the year[cite: 16]
options.B: Capitalized as part of fixed assets
options.C: Adjusted against general reserve directly
options.D: Ignored until final liquidation

answer_html: Answer: (A) In the absence of details of the term, the entire redemption premium is charged to the profit and loss account of the year[cite: 16].
topic_text: Treatment of Premium on Redemption of Debentures

question_html: Can unlisted NBFCs for privately placed debentures be required to maintain a 10% DRR?

options.A: Yes, 10% DRR is mandatory for all unlisted NBFCs.
options.B: No DRR is required for privately placed debentures of unlisted NBFCs[cite: 16].
options.C: 25% DRR is required.
options.D: 50% DRR is required.

answer_html: Answer: (B) All unlisted NBFCs and HFCs for privately placed debentures require no DRR[cite: 16].
topic_text: DRR for Unlisted NBFCs and HFCs

question_html: What rule and year governs the adequacy and investment of Debenture Redemption Reserve under the Companies Act?

options.A: Rule 18(7) of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Amendment Rules, 2019[cite: 16]
options.B: Rule 12(3) of Companies Incorporation Rules, 2014
options.C: Section 55 of Companies Act, 2013
options.D: Rule 9 of Companies Audit Rules, 2014

answer_html: Answer: (A) Rule 18(7) of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Amendment Rules, 2019 covers DRR adequacy and investment[cite: 16].

question_html: What does the term 'Redeemable debentures' imply?

options.A: Debentures that are never repaid during the company's lifetime.
options.B: Debentures that are either redeemed in cash or convertible to equity shares after a time period[cite: 16].
options.C: Debentures that carry permanent voting rights.
options.D: Debentures that can be cancelled without payment.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Redeemable debentures are redeemed in cash or converted to equity shares after a time period[cite: 16].

question_html: If a company fails to pay interest on debentures when due, what can the Tribunal do upon application?

options.A: Direct the company to redeem the debentures forthwith by payment of principal and interest due[cite: 16]
options.B: Order compulsory liquidation of the company immediately
options.C: Waive all interest liabilities permanently
options.D: Transfer management to the Registrar of Companies

answer_html: Answer: (A) The Tribunal may direct the company to redeem the debentures forthwith by payment of principal and interest due[cite: 16].

question_html: What is the accounting entry for transfer of interest on DRR investments to Profit and Loss Account?

options.A: Interest on DRR Investment A/c Dr. To Profit and Loss A/c[cite: 16]
options.B: Profit and Loss A/c Dr. To Interest on DRR Investment A/c
options.C: Bank A/c Dr. To Interest on DRRI A/c
options.D: DRR A/c Dr. To Interest on DRRI A/c

answer_html: Answer: (A) Interest on DRR Investment Account is debited and Profit and Loss Account is credited[cite: 16].
topic_text: Journal Entry for Interest on DRRI Transfer

question_html: When can appropriation to DRR and investment in specified securities be made in practice according to advisory guidelines for ease?

options.A: Immediately after debentures are allotted, assuming sufficient profits[cite: 16]
options.B: Only on the exact date of redemption maturity
options.C: After the financial year has ended and audited
options.D: Only with SEBI prior written consent

answer_html: Answer: (A) For simplicity and ease, it is advisable to make appropriation and investment immediately after debentures are allotted[cite: 16].
topic_text: Timing of DRR Appropriation and Investment

question_html: What does Section 71(4) of the Companies Act, 2013 mandate regarding debentures?

options.A: Creation of a debenture redemption reserve account out of profits available for dividend[cite: 16]
options.B: Prohibition of issuing debentures at a discount
options.C: Mandatory conversion of all debentures into equity within 3 years
options.D: Requirement of RBI approval for every debenture issue

answer_html: Answer: (A) Section 71(4) mandates creating a debenture redemption reserve account out of profits available for dividend[cite: 16].

question_html: What must happen to the amount remaining deposited or invested as DRR investment during the year?

options.A: It shall not at any time fall below 15% of the amount of debentures maturing during the 31st day of March of that year[cite: 16].
options.B: It can be withdrawn completely once a month.
options.C: It must be increased to 100% of total debentures.
options.D: It can be transferred to general reserve before maturity.

answer_html: Answer: (A) The amount remaining deposited or invested shall not at any time fall below 15% of the amount of debentures maturing[cite: 16].

question_html: What is the accounting entry for receipt of interest on Debenture Redemption Reserve Investments?

options.A: Bank A/c Dr. To Interest on Debenture Redemption Reserve Investment A/c[cite: 16]
options.B: Interest on DRRI A/c Dr. To Bank A/c
options.C: DRR Investment A/c Dr. To Bank A/c
options.D: Bank A/c Dr. To DRR A/c

answer_html: Answer: (A) Bank Account is debited and Interest on Debenture Redemption Reserve Investment Account is credited[cite: 16].
topic_text: Journal Entry for Interest Receipt on DRRI

question_html: Which companies other than AIFIs, Banking Companies, and FIs are required to invest 15% of maturing debentures by April 30th?

options.A: All listed NBFCs, all listed HFCs, all other listed companies, and all unlisted companies which are not NBFCs and HFCs[cite: 16]
options.B: Only unlisted manufacturing companies with over ₹10 crore capital
options.C: Only government-owned public sector undertakings
options.D: All companies without exception

answer_html: Answer: (A) Listed NBFCs, listed HFCs, other listed companies, and unlisted non-NBFC/HFC companies must invest 15%[cite: 16].

question_html: What does the term 'Fixed charge' on assets mean in relation to debentures?

options.A: It is a charge on specific, identified fixed assets of the company.
options.B: It is a shifting charge on all current assets of the company.
options.C: It is a charge on the future profits only.
options.D: It is an unsecured guarantee by the directors.

answer_html: Answer: (A) A fixed charge is created on specific assets described in the debenture deed[cite: 16].

question_html: If a company issues debentures redeemable after a fixed number of years, what is this method of redemption called?

options.A: Redemption after a fixed number of years[cite: 16]
options.B: Redemption by open market purchase
options.C: Redemption by annual drawing
options.D: Redemption on demand

answer_html: Answer: (A) Redeemable debentures may be redeemed after a fixed number of years[cite: 16].

question_html: What is printed on the bond certificate regarding the charge on assets?

options.A: The Registrar's certificate registering the charge[cite: 16]
options.B: The personal signatures of all equity shareholders
options.C: The SEBI Chairman's approval stamp
options.D: The annual profit and loss figures

answer_html: Answer: (A) Since the charge is not valid unless registered with the Registrar, his certificate registering the charge is printed on the bond[cite: 16].

question_html: What is the accounting entry for transferring DRR to General Reserve upon redemption?

options.A: Debenture Redemption Reserve A/c Dr. To General Reserve[cite: 16]
options.B: General Reserve A/c Dr. To DRR A/c
options.C: Profit and Loss A/c Dr. To General Reserve A/c
options.D: Debentures A/c Dr. To General Reserve A/c

answer_html: Answer: (A) Debenture Redemption Reserve Account is debited and General Reserve is credited[cite: 16].
topic_text: Journal Entry for DRR Transfer to General Reserve

question_html: When are debentures considered redeemed according to the terms of issue?

options.A: When the principal debt and any applicable premium/interest are fully paid off or converted[cite: 16]
options.B: Immediately upon passing a board resolution
options.C: When DRR investments are purchased
options.D: When the prospectus is filed with RoC

answer_html: Answer: (A) Redemption must be done according to terms of issue by paying off debt or converting[cite: 16].

question_html: What happens if a company fails to redeem debentures on the date of maturity?

options.A: The Tribunal may direct the company to redeem the debentures forthwith upon application by holders or trustees[cite: 16].
options.B: The company is automatically granted a 5-year extension.
options.C: Debentures are converted into preference shares by law.
options.D: The board of directors is dissolved automatically.

answer_html: Answer: (A) The Tribunal may direct the company to redeem the debentures forthwith upon application[cite: 16].

question_html: What is another name commonly used for Debenture Redemption Reserve Investment?

options.A: Debenture Redemption Fund[cite: 16]
options.B: Capital Redemption Reserve
options.C: Securities Premium Reserve
options.D: General Sinking Account

answer_html: Answer: (A) Investment is termed as Debenture Redemption Reserve Investment (or Debenture Redemption Fund)[cite: 16].
